Facts: A widow claimed ownership by adverse possession of an apartment occupied continuously since 1976, originally belonging to a deceased owner without heirs, allegedly devolved to the State as a vacant inheritance.
Legal framework
Articles 1158–1167, 480 and 586 of the Italian Civil Code on adverse possession, limitation for acceptance of inheritance and State succession; Article 1(260) Law no. 296/2006; Legislative Decree no. 42/2004 on cultural heritage.
Interpretative issue
Whether long-term possession of property devolved to the State as a vacant inheritance can mature into adverse possession, and whether notification to the State Property Agency under Law no. 296/2006 is required for possession commenced before 2007.
Principle applied
Ordinary adverse possession of immovable property requires continuous, peaceful, public and unequivocal possession uti dominus for twenty years. Law no. 296/2006 has no retroactive effect; therefore, failure to notify the State Property Agency is irrelevant for possession commenced and matured before its entry into force. Property devolved to the State under Article 586 ICC is subject to adverse possession unless it is proven to belong to the inalienable public domain. Absent proof of cultural or historical constraints, prolonged possession satisfying statutory requirements results in acquisition of ownership by adverse possession.
